{{Short description|Potential cohort of Generation Alpha}}
'''Coronials''' (sometimes called '''Generation C''' which is often shortened to '''Gen C''')<ref>{{Cite news |last=Shoichet |first=Catherine E. |date=March 11, 2021 |title=Meet Gen C, the Covid Generation |url=https://www.cnn.com/2021/03/11/us/covid-generation-gen-c/index.html |access-date=May 21, 2024 |work=[[CNN]]}}</ref> is a term used to describe those conceived in the wake of the [[coronavirus pandemic]] (2020–2023).  

==Background==
Similarly to [[population growth]] following the initial decline in population due to natural disasters or war, such as [[Second World War]] [[baby boomers]], coronials are conceived in one of two situations: increased sexual activity between self-isolated or locked-down couples,<ref>{{Cite news |last=Maloy |first=Ashley Fretters |date=December 20, 2020 |title=Conceived in a pandemic, born in a pandemic: The first quarantine babies are arriving |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/lifestyle/2020/12/24/first-pandemic-quarantine-babies/ |archive-date= |access-date=May 19, 2024 |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]}}</ref> or population growth following the demise of the infection; which has been encouraged amongst some communities and governments.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.dailysabah.com/world/europe/coronials-zelenskiy-urges-ukrainians-to-make-babies-in-covid-19-quarantine | title=Coronials: Zelenskiy urges Ukrainians to make babies in COVID-19 quarantine | website=[[Daily Sabah]] | date=17 March 2020 }}</ref>

==Origins==
The name "coronials" is derived from the [[coronavirus]] and its affiliated pandemic, and the demographic group, [[Millennials]]. The term was mentioned on the [[This Week in Virology]] podcast in April 2020 as an alternative name for [[Generation Z|Gen Z]], which was characterized as "a totally lame name".  It was stated that the pandemic is a "defining event for what is being called Gen Z".<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Dove |first1=Alan |last2=Barker |first2=Brianne |last3=Griffin |first3=Daniel |last4=Despommier |first4=Dickson |last5=Spindler |first5=Kathy |last6=Condit |first6=Rich |last7=Racaniello |first7=Vincent |date=April 12, 2020 |title=SARS-CoV-2 – Enter the Coronials |url=https://asm.org/Podcasts/TWiV/Episodes/SARS-CoV-2-enter-the-Coronials-TWiV-600 |access-date=2024-05-19 |website=ASM.org |at=Time index 41:43 |language=en |type=Podcast}}</ref>

A ''[[Nurse Education Today]]'' paper in 2020 suggested that the term might be better applied to the [[Cohort (statistics)|cohort]] of nurses who completed their training during the pandemic.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Montoforte-Royo |first1=Cristina |last2=Fuster |first2=Pilar |date=November 2020 |title=Coronials: Nurses who graduated during the COVID-19 pandemic. Will they be better nurses? |journal=[[Nurse Education Today]] |volume=94 |doi=10.1016/j.nedt.2020.104536 |pmid=32801065 |pmc=7387935 }}</ref>  Chip Le Grand of ''[[The Sydney Morning Herald]]'' used the term to refer to "the generation of young people who finished high school and started uni in the COVID lockdown years".<ref>{{Cite news |last=Le Grand |first=Chip |date=February 26, 2024 |title=If we want more young people to go to uni, stop screwing them over |url=https://www.smh.com.au/national/if-we-want-more-young-people-to-go-to-uni-stop-screwing-them-over-20240225-p5f7ms.html |access-date=May 19, 2024 |work=[[The Sydney Morning Herald]]}}</ref>

==Alternative definition==
The term may also be used to describe those of Generations [[Generation Z|Z]] and [[Generation Alpha|Alpha]] whose adolescent lives have been significantly impacted by the social effects of the pandemic.  One such impact is that of school closures which began in March 2020 in several countries as part of precautionary measures to stop the spread of the virus.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-51952314 | title=UK schools to close from Friday | date=18 March 2020 }}</ref>  Those students whose examinations would not have taken place, for example those in the [[United Kingdom]]<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.bbc.com/news/education-51980831 | title=Coronavirus: Teachers to estimate grades after exams cancelled | date=20 March 2020 }}</ref> may be referred to as coronials.
